item.title: Australia Home Sales Rise in Fledgling Sign of Property Recovery
item.description: Australian home sales and auction clearance rates climbed, offering hopes of a recovery for a property market that has slumped as interest rates rose this year.
item.dc:creator: Richard Henderson

item.title: Meta’s $25 Billion Bond Sale Highlights Shifting Landscape for Tech Debt
item.description: Selling billions of dollars of corporate bonds on Election Day seemed like a real gamble.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia

item.title: Top Turkish Regulators Taken Into Custody in Fund Probe
item.description: Turkish authorities detained top officials from the country’s regulators on Saturday, local media reported, the latest executives to be caught up in a widening fund scandal.
item.dc:creator: Murat Oztaskin

item.title: New Chief of Staff, Chain Reaction Tech Selloff
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Yorkville Ives & Co. Partner & Senior Managing Director Dan Ives, Rutgers-Eagleton Center for Public Interest Polling Director Ashley Koning, PNC Asset Management Group Chief Investment Officer Amanda Agati, Travel Journalist Brittany Chang, Atlanta Journal-Constitution Washington Bureau Chief Tia Mitchell, ​​General Catalyst Chairman & Managing Director Ken Chenault and Composer & Pianist Missy Mazzoli. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway Boosts Buybacks as Operating Income Slips
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. spent about $9.6 billion to buy back its own shares in the third quarter, a sign the company’s executives viewed the stock as undervalued. But declining insurance underwriting weighed on its operating earnings in a mixed quarter for the company.
item.dc:creator: Alex Rajbhandari

item.title: Ken Chenault on Leadership in an Age of AI
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, General Catalyst Chairman and Managing Director and former American Express CEO Ken Chenault discusses leadership, diversity and responsible AI, arguing that executives need the courage to stand by their values even as political and technological pressures intensify. Chenault tells host David Gura that companies should pursue innovation while protecting safety, broadening opportunity and ensuring AI ultimately improves people's lives. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: A Historic First for Women at the Metropolitan Opera
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, composer Missy Mazzoli discusses adapting George Saunders's Lincoln in the Bardo and becoming the first woman composer to have a world premiere at the Metropolitan Opera. Mazzoli tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini how punk helped shape her musical sensibility and why her long collaboration with librettist Royce Vavrek was essential to transforming Saunders's sprawling ghost story into an opera. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How the Iran War Is Making Alaskans Both Richer and Poorer
item.description: Oil prices have surged across the United States as a result of the ongoing war in Iran. This means higher costs for households in most states, but in Alaska, the state government is bringing in new revenue from its high oil production to offset those higher costs. Some of the revenue is then redistributed to Alaskans through the state’s unique sovereign wealth fund. While most Americans disapprove of the war in Iran, Alaska may emerge as a quiet winner from one of the conflict’s most painful economic side effects: higher oil prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Protein Craze Fuels an Investment Boom in Livestock Health
item.description: Animal health companies are tapping into the protein craze, investing billions of dollars to build up businesses focused on making cattle, pigs and poultry healthier for human consumption.
item.dc:creator: Ilena Peng
